paper.title: An Efficient Minimax-Optimal Algorithm for Adversarial $m$-Set Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial m-set bandits (action-normalized losses, adaptive non-anticipating adversary)
unmapped: Actions are all m-subsets of d items, K = binom(d,m); learner observes only the aggregate loss <X_t, l_t> (full-bandit combinatorial feedback)
Adversary chooses l_t F_{t-1}-measurably (may see p_t but not the draw X_t)
Realized regret against best fixed m-set; |<x,l_t>| <= 1 for all actions
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t\in[T]$, the learner selects an $\mathcal F_{t-1}$-measurable distribution $p_t\in\Delta(\cX)$ ... The adversary selects a loss vector $\ell_t\in\mathbb R^d$ that is also $\mathcal F_{t-1}$-measurable. ... The learner then draws $X_t\sim p_t$ and observes only the loss $Y_t:=\langle X_t,\ell_t\rangle.$ We use the standard action-level normalization $|\langle x,\ell_t\rangle|\le 1$

|<x, l_t>| <= 1 for all actions x
tuning: eta = min{1/(256 d), sqrt(log(12K/delta)/(320 d T))}

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: There exists a universal constant $C>0$ such that the following holds. Let $T\ge1$ be an integer, let $\delta\in(0,1)$, and assume $1\le m\le d-1$. Run \Cref{alg:exp3-kw}. Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, \[ R_T \le C\sqrt{ dT\left( \log K+\log\frac1\delta \right) }, \] where $K=\binom{d}{m}$. One may take $C=160$.

results.notes: Realized regret bounded with probability 1-delta. Implementation runs in T*poly(d,m,log T) time (Proposition prop:efficient-implementation). Implies O~(sqrt(d s T)), s=min(m,d-m).

bound.regime: delta in (0, delta_0], T >= frak_T(d,m,delta) polynomial in d, m, log(1/delta)

conditions: K = binom(d,m)
regret exceeds the bound with probability at least delta

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: There exist universal constants $c>0$ and $\delta_0\in(0,1)$ and a threshold $\mathfrak T(d,m,\delta)$ bounded by a polynomial in $d$, $m$, and $\log(1/\delta)$ such that ... For every randomized policy on $\cX_{d,m}$, there exists a deterministic adaptive non-anticipating loss process whose action losses belong to $[0,1]$ and such that \[ \Pp ( R_T\ge c\sqrt{dT(\log\binom dm+\log\frac1\delta)} )\ge\delta. \]

results.notes: Statement is P(R_T >= bound) >= delta; recorded as high-probability regret lower bound.

bound.regime: delta in (0, 2^{-36}], T >= ceil(d^2 + 64 d s log(e d/s) + 4 d s^2 log(1/delta))

conditions: K = binom(d,m)
regret exceeds the bound with probability at least delta

source.label: thm:lower-bound-explicit
source.quote: Let $d\ge2$, let $1\le m\le d-1$, and set $s:=\min\{m,d-m\}$. Let $\delta\in(0,2^{-36}]$, and assume that $T \ge \lceil d^2 +64d s\log\frac{ed}{s} +4d s^2\log\frac1\delta \rceil$. Then, for every randomized policy on $\cX_{d,m}$, there exists a deterministic adaptive non-anticipating loss process whose action losses belong to $[0,1]$ and such that \[ \Pp( R_T \ge 2^{-39} \sqrt{dT( \log\binom dm+ \log\frac1\delta )} ) \ge \delta. \]

results.notes: Explicit appendix version of thm:lower-bound; printed number 'Theorem 1' per annotation.

bound.regime: delta in (0, delta_0], T >= frak_T_MAB(K,delta) polynomial in K and log(1/delta)

conditions: regret exceeds the bound with probability at least delta

source.label: cor:ordinary-bandits-lower-bound
source.quote: There exist universal constants $c>0$ and $\delta_0\in(0,1)$ and a threshold $\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{MAB}}(K,\delta)$ bounded by a polynomial in $K$ and $\log(1/\delta)$ such that ... For every randomized $K$-armed bandit policy, there exists a deterministic adaptive non-anticipating loss process $\ell_t\in[0,1]^K$ such that \[ \Pp ( R_T\ge c\sqrt{KT(\log K+\log\frac1\delta)} )\ge\delta. \]

results.notes: m=1, d=K specialization; explicit constants c=2^-39, delta_0=2^-36 follow from Theorem 1.

bound.regime: floor(d/m) >= 2^32, T >= 64 d m log(e d/m)

conditions: paper's (n,k) mapped to (d,m) with 1 <= m <= d/2
K = binom(d,m)
regret exceeds the bound with probability at least 2^-10

source.label: prop:lower-sparse-action
source.quote: Let $1\le k\le n/2$, let $r:=\lfloor n/k\rfloor\ge r_\star=2^{32}$, and suppose that $T \ge 64nk\log\frac{en}{k}$. For every randomized policy on $\mathcal X_{n,k}$, there exists a deterministic adaptive non-anticipating loss process with every action loss in $[0,1]$ such that \Pp( R_T \ge 2^{-31}\sqrt{nT\log\binom nk} ) \ge 2^{-10}.

results.notes: Constant-probability (2^-10) lower bound; recorded as realized_regret.

conditions: paper's (n,k) mapped to (d,m) with 1 <= m <= d/2
K = binom(d,m)
regret exceeds the bound with probability at least 2^-14

source.label: prop:lower-bounded-action
source.quote: Let $1\le k\le n/2$, assume $\lfloor n/k\rfloor<r_\star=2^{32}$, and let $T\ge n^2$. For every randomized policy on $\mathcal X_{n,k}$, there exists a deterministic loss sequence fixed in advance, with every action loss in $[0,1]$, such that \Pp( R_T \ge 2^{-38}\sqrt{nT\log\binom nk} ) \ge 2^{-14}.

results.notes: Holds against an oblivious (fixed in advance) loss sequence; constant probability 2^-14.

bound.regime: T >= max{d^2, 64 d m log(e d/m)}

conditions: paper's (n,k) mapped to (d,m) with 1 <= m <= d/2
K = binom(d,m)
regret exceeds the bound with probability at least 2^-14

source.label: cor:lower-action-count
source.quote: Let $1\le k\le n/2$ and suppose that $T \ge \max\{ n^2, 64nk\log\frac{en}{k} \}$. For every randomized policy on $\mathcal X_{n,k}$, there exists a deterministic adaptive non-anticipating loss process with every action loss in $[0,1]$ such that \Pp( R_T \ge 2^{-38}\sqrt{nT\log\binom nk} ) \ge 2^{-14}.

results.notes: Combines Propositions 1 and 2; constant-probability lower bound.

conditions: paper's (n,k) mapped to (d,m) with 1 <= m <= d/2
regret exceeds the bound with probability at least delta

source.label: prop:lower-confidence
source.quote: Let $1\le k\le n/2$, let $0<\delta\le2^{-36}$, and suppose that $T \ge 4nk^2\log\frac1\delta$. For every randomized policy on $\mathcal X_{n,k}$, there exists a deterministic adaptive non-anticipating loss process with every action loss in $[0,1]$ such that \Pp( R_T \ge 2^{-17}\sqrt{nT\log\frac1\delta} ) \ge \delta.
